title: Recognizing the Origin of a Speaker

blocks.text: Now you know the fuṣḥā, the Egyptian, the Levant (passive) and the Moroccan (passive). But the Arab world speaks of many other varieties: the Gulf, Iraq, Sudan, Tunisia, Algeria, Libya and Yemen. You can't learn all of them; But you can learn to recognize them: just a dozen words and some sounds are enough to say, most likely, this speaker comes from the Maghreb or this is an accent of the Gulf. It is a useful skill to understand (know what to expect), to translate (B2-17: The choice of variety is information) and to work with open sources. But it is also a skill to use with caution: an accent indicates a probability, not an identity. In this unit you learn the large dialect areas, a table of traits (G77), a three-step method and the correct way to report a hypothesis on variety. A new character accompanies you: Ġāda, Tunisian journalist. Three weeks, in parallel with MAG-02.

Targets. At the end of the lesson you know:
1. describe the great dialectal areas of the Arab world;
2. use a table of strokes (sounds, grammar words, verb) to recognize the area of a speaker;
3. to distinguish, at least broadly, the varieties of the Maghreb and those of the Gulf and Iraq;
4. to know what factors make a hypothesis (adaptment, mobility, media, mixed varieties) uncertain;
5. refer a hypothesis on the variety with the correct degree of certainty, in English and Arabic.
